text:
maria: quick sync — i'm prototyping a compact token-muxing approach at the frontdoor to cut per-tenant memory and simplify eviction. main question: central coordinator vs hashed local shards for credit accounting?
vikram: central coord = single point of tail-latency failure. i prefer local shards with periodic global reconciliation. cheaper on p99. :eyes:
olivia: local shards + CRDT-like counters could work. eventual consistency ok as long as reconciliation window is bounded and we have good metrics.
jamal: local-only opens abuse window during partitions — a malicious tenant could spike and consume more credits before reconcile. we need a short-lived hard cap.
lena: +1 on hybrid. local muxing for fast path, backed by a lightweight ledger service that accepts batched writes for global corrections. leaderless reconcile to avoid a single leader.
raj: migration wise — wrap token envelope with a version field and compat layer in proxies. rollout via canary and per-region opt-in. metrics to watch: rejected-rate, reconcilation-delta, p99 ingress latency.
maria: memory compaction idea: pack tenant metadata into a 64-bit header and keep KV cache in sharded arenas. cold tenants get offloaded to redis/rocks with async refill. keeps hot path in L1.
vikram: agree. also add bucketed short-burst admission: allow bursts up to 3x for a 200ms window, then enforce smoothing. reduces tail for spiky workloads.
olivia: we should capture these as measurable SLOs: token-drift (tokens seen locally vs global), reconcile-latency, lost-credit-rate. add alerts for >2% drift.
jamal: security note: sign token envelopes with KMS to prevent replay when proxies operate offline. also replay nonce + lease expiry.
lena: can we run synthetic abuse tests? i can extend the load harness to simulate partition + aggressive tenants. will need a staging ledger with dump/restore.
maria: sample proxy config i sketched:
```
proxy.token_mux:
  mode: hybrid
  reconcile_interval_ms: 5000
  burst_window_ms: 200
  burst_multiplier: 3
  offload_store: redis://token-ledger-staging
```
maria: i'll draft an RFC with state-machine diagrams, migration steps, and performance targets. ping me with anything to add. :thumbsup: 
raj: nits — define exact semantics for "reconcile" (merge vs overwrite) and whether ledger is authoritative. also spell out retry/backoff policy.
infra-bot: deploy-bot: canary started for mux-v2 on infra-canary-3 at 2025-10-05T10:23Z
maria: thanks — i’ll include the reconcile semantics and backoff table in the RFC. planning to share a first draft tomorrow.
